events.title: Telegram
events.text:
I never understood why Americans, and well, not just Americans but also others from developed countries have this insatiable thirst of individualism, in the case of North America it is slightly understandable since they have no civilization to lay their weight on, but at a point it does not limit itself to new or old societies, only about the natural pridefulness of man.
I met again an old friend, he got out based on psychiatric reasons, and as we were drinking tea we were reminding ourselves of the tales from what happened and what we saw, and he reminded me of what happened at his blockpost, we got a good laugh out of it and then I felt bad.
Well, this guy, a Bedouin, goes to the checkpoint with his truck - a tank and two dozen guys at arms are guarding it, one asks him to submit to inspection and the Bedouin flatly says "No.". You have to understand that this was years in the war, and the idea that somebody would say "No." to a simple thing like an inspection that would not last more than three minutes was just dumbfounded.
Then my friend goes out in his tank top and his shorts and asks what's the matter, just let us inspect your truck, and the guy kept saying no, and this brought that and they argued and the guy had the intellect to say phrases like "You are not going to see the tomorrows sunlight." and "You are all going to die."
To this day I am unsure of why he did it, tribal pride? Was he smuggling dildos to Israel? maybe a secret smugglers to the black flags? just why? Maybe an argument with the wife that made him unpleasant in conversation?
It did not matter to my friend, who immediately left and returned with his automatic and shot him.
Of course, investigation later showed this guy was no smuggler to suspicious characters, he was a local guy and belonged to so and so tribe.
So we return to the main question - why do people just refuse to submit? It was not like we were asking to inspect his woman or his daughter, or we were humiliating him in some way, why do Americans argue with their cops if they were at fault or when its procedures? Why are some people completely neurotic to the concept of yielding to such basic things? I cant kick his corpse back up and ask him what he was thinking, that retard.
Well, I laughed, then I felt bad about myself because it was not proper to do so, strange how after such things you feel more meek and polite towards people instead of being irritating and aggravating.

📈 Oil prices climb as Middle East risks mount ahead of OPEC+ meeting
Brent and WTI are heading for their first weekly gains this month as renewed threats to Middle Eastern oil supplies fuel market uncertainty, the WSJ reports.
Brent rose 0.6% to $97.15 a barrel on Friday, while US WTI jumped 2.7% to $85.96.
The rally comes amid fresh attacks on energy infrastructure: a strike on Saudi Arabia’s Jazan refinery sparked a fire and temporarily halted some operations, while a drone attack in Kuwait killed two Italian technicians.
👉 Traders are also watching Sunday's OPEC+ meeting, where producers are expected to discuss output policy for 2027. Disruptions caused by the war against Iran have complicated efforts to assess production capacity and set quotas.
Whether the group restores supply, maintains current restrictions or considers further cuts remains unclear. But for now, geopolitical risks are overshadowing the upcoming OPEC+ decision.

Tech giants are outbidding US defense contractors for materials, factory space, energy critical supplies, and scarce workers, the FT has reported.
The US push to ramp up weapons and aircraft production is colliding with the AI infrastructure boom, with both competing for the same strained manufacturing capacity.
🌏 defense contractors are under pressure to increase munitions production as the Iran war and [Ukraine aid drain stocks](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/75955)

🇫🇷 Le Pen win could trigger Frexit, says French minister 
A potential Marine Le Pen presidency could pull France out of the European Union, the Financial Times cites French Minister Delegate for European Affairs Benjamin Haddad as saying. 
He argues that France’s right-wing National Rally party - where Marine Le Pen leads the parliamentary group -could lead the country toward a hidden or de facto “Frexit.” 
In his opinion, a National Rally government would inevitably set France on a collision course with Brussels, with the first major struggles likely erupting over the EU budget and financial aid to Ukraine. 
France’s presidential election is scheduled for April 18, 2027, with a second round set for May 2 if required. 
Le Pen maintains a huge lead - a Toluna-Harris Interactive survey, conducted for French media outlets, put her at around 31% of voting intentions across the first-round scenarios tested.
Her main potential challenger is Jean-Luc Melenchon, the leader of the left-wing France Unbowed (LFI) party, who is also seen as a strong contender to reach the runoff.

events.title: Telegram
events.text:
🪖 EU seeks fresh billions to replace US military muscle
 
The EU is preparing tens of billions of dollars in new loans and grants to reduce its dependence on US military capabilities, Bloomberg reports, citing sources.
 
Accelerating the drive towards military autonomy under the banner of countering [a mythical ‘Russian threat’](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76914), the proposed funding package, expected to launch in the second half of 2027, would build on last year’s ≈ $165 billion SAFE military loan scheme.
 
Its focus would be on capabilities European armies still heavily depend on the US to provide.
Priority areas reportedly include:
➡️ integrated air and missile defense
➡️ intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance
➡️ strategic transport, logistics and operational coordination needed to deploy and sustain forces
 
The funding package would reportedly combine EU borrowing with allocations from the bloc’s next seven-year budget.
Brussels’ plans face financial hurdles: negotiations have already cut proposed defense and space funding in the EU’s 2028–2034 budget by 30%.
The original budget proposal earmarked around $152 billion for defense, with roughly half intended for strategic enablers - precisely the capabilities Europe now says it urgently needs.
The push comes as the[ Trump administration scales back ](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/77780)some US rapid-reaction forces and military equipment stationed in Europe.
👍 [Substack](https://geopoliticsprime.substack.com/) | [Chat](https://t.me/+HLrnOk92f31mYzIy) |

events.text:
🇺🇸🇨🇳 US influence wanes as Southeast Asia embraces China’s drone tech
Regional countries are increasingly turning to China for affordable drone technology as they seek to diversify their defense capabilities rather than rely solely on Western suppliers, reports Bloomberg.
China’s advantage goes beyond competitive prices: it offers technology transfers, local production partnerships and access to systems that the US has often been reluctant to export.
Several regional militaries are already combining Chinese technology with Western and other foreign equipment:
♦️ Thailand, a major Non-NATO Ally, operates imported American and Swedish combat aircraft and helicopters armed with South Korean guided bombs, alongside Chinese T-4 main battle tanks and VN-1 armored vehicles. It also uses Chinese-designed UAVs like the Wing Loong series and has developed domestic drones based on Chinese technology.
♦️ Indonesia uses Chinese and Turkish drones while expanding its arsenal with Indian cruise missiles.
♦️ The Philippines is integrating Israeli and Australian equipment into its military capabilities, including for surveillance operations in the South China Sea.
♦️ Myanmar’s conflict has also demonstrated the growing importance of unmanned systems on the battlefield.
China’s influence extends well beyond finished military drones, the publication underscores. It dominates the global commercial drone market, worth over $5 billion annually, and supplies critical components underpinning the wider industry.
👍 [Substack](https://geopoliticsprime.substack.com/) | [Chat](https://t.me/+HLrnOk92f31mYzIy) |

events.text:
🇮🇱🇹🇷🇸🇾Israel sees emerging Turkey-Syria alliance as regional threat
The Israeli security establishment is increasingly concerned that closer Turkish-Syrian ties could expand Ankara’s regional influence at Tel Aviv’s expense, The Jerusalem Post reports.
🔴 Israel’s Military Intelligence Directorate and Mossad are closely monitoring a series of reciprocal diplomatic visits by Syrian and Turkish officials amid rising tensions over [Israeli military operations in southern Syria.](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/77810)
🔴 The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) fears Turkey could deploy radars and air defense systems in northern Syria, restricting Israeli Air Force operations there and complicating strikes on Iran, for which Israeli aircraft [use Syrian airspace as a transit route](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76551).
🔴 Turkey has begun clearing mines in Gaziantep Province to rehabilitate the historic Hejaz Railway and restore its link to Syria’s Aleppo Province. Israeli defense officials see Ankara’s infrastructure projects as an effort to re-establish Turkey as a gateway to the Middle East, threatening Israeli interests and Tel Aviv’s proposed India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC)
🔴 Israel also views the possible expansion of the Mecca Pact to[ include Syria as a setback](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/77907). Damascus is seeking to join the broader Arab and Muslim community and develop a railway corridor through Jordan to Saudi Arabia, potentially extending to Gulf states and Europe as part of the ambitious Hejaz Railway project
🔴 Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan’s son Bilal Erdogan recently traveled to Beirut, a move seen by Tel Aviv as an attempt to expand Turkey’s influence in Lebanon
🔴 Turkey has also asked US President Donald Trump to let Ankara participate in Gaza’s reconstruction — a move Israel strongly opposes
The Israeli press reports that these developments could prompt the IDF to reinforce its troop deployments in the region and [adjust its operational posture.](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/78155)
